items.title: Pure budget-policy resolution + over-budget predicate
items.context: In core/usage-ledger/dispatch-usage.ts add a pure resolveHardBudget(env) that reads LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS (fallback KOALA_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS), parses a positive integer, returns { hardBudgetTokens: number, budgetPolicyId: string } | null (null when unset/invalid -> no enforcement). Add a pure isOverHardBudget(estimatedInputTokens, hardBudgetTokens) -> boolean. Unit-tested: unset -> null (no enforcement); valid -> policy; estimate over/under the ceiling.

happy.desc: resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"5000"}) -> {hardBudgetTokens:5000, budgetPolicyId:"hard-budget:5000"}; WHY: canonical positive-integer parse + policy id shape
isOverHardBudget(6000, 5000) -> true; WHY: estimate exceeds ceiling, must return true
isOverHardBudget(4000, 5000) -> false; WHY: estimate within ceiling, must return false

edge.desc: resolveHardBudget({}) (no LATTICE_ or KOALA_ env) -> null; WHY: unset means no enforcement, null disables budget gate
resolveHardBudget({KOALA_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"3000"}) with no LATTICE_ -> reads KOALA_ fallback -> {hardBudgetTokens:3000,...}; WHY: legacy compat migration path
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"7000",KOALA_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"3000"}) -> uses LATTICE_ (7000), ignores KOALA_; WHY: LATTICE_ takes precedence over legacy fallback
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"0"}) -> null; WHY: zero is not a positive integer, means no enforcement
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"-100"}) -> null; WHY: negative is invalid, no enforcement
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"abc"}) -> null; WHY: non-numeric string is invalid, no enforcement
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"3.14"}) -> null; WHY: float is not a positive integer, no enforcement
isOverHardBudget(5000, 5000) -> false; WHY: exact boundary (estimate == budget) must NOT block, only strict exceed blocks
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"1"}) -> {hardBudgetTokens:1,...}; WHY: minimum valid positive integer accepted
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"  5000  "}) -> either null or {hardBudgetTokens:5000,...}; WHY: leading/trailing whitespace handling must be explicit and not crash

adversarial.desc: resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"9007199254740992"}) -> null or valid; WHY: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1 would lose precision, must not silently accept unsafe integer
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"Infinity"}) -> null; WHY: Infinity parses as number but is not a finite positive integer
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:"NaN"}) -> null; WHY: NaN parses but is not a valid integer
resolveHardBudget({LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS:""}) -> null; WHY: empty string is not a valid budget
isOverHardBudget(0, 5000) -> false; WHY: zero estimate (empty prompt) is within any positive budget
resolveHardBudget never throws for any env shape; WHY: must be crash-proof to avoid blocking dispatch on a parse error

items.title: buildBlockedBudgetRecord (pure, validated)
items.context: Add buildBlockedBudgetRecord(model, estimateResult, correlation, attribution, budgetPolicyId, reasonCode) parallel to buildUnavailableFinalRecord: a record with decision.kind='blocked', budgetPolicyId, reasonCode (e.g. 'hard_budget_exceeded'), usage.source='prompt-size-estimate' (the estimate that triggered the block) or 'unavailable', supersedesRecordIds=[estimateRecordId]. It MUST pass validateUsageLedgerRecord. Never throws. Tested: produces a valid blocked record; decision.kind is blocked; supersedes the estimate.

happy.desc: buildBlockedBudgetRecord(model, estimateResult, correlation, attribution, "hard-budget:5000", "hard_budget_exceeded") -> record with decision.kind=="blocked"; WHY: primary contract: a budget block must record kind=blocked
buildBlockedBudgetRecord -> record.budgetPolicyId == passed budgetPolicyId; WHY: blocked record must carry the policy that triggered the block for audit trail
buildBlockedBudgetRecord -> record.decision.reasonCode == "hard_budget_exceeded"; WHY: reason code must be preserved for diagnostics
buildBlockedBudgetRecord -> record.supersedesRecordIds contains the estimateRecordId; WHY: the blocked record supersedes the estimate so summary never double-counts
buildBlockedBudgetRecord output passes validateUsageLedgerRecord({expectIntegrity:false}) with ok:true; WHY: load-bearing invariant -- blocked records must be schema-valid

edge.desc: buildBlockedBudgetRecord never throws even with minimal/edge inputs; WHY: parallels buildUnavailableFinalRecord contract -- never propagate error to dispatch

buildBlockedBudgetRecord -> usage.source is prompt-size-estimate or unavailable (NOT provider-reported); WHY: a blocked call never reached the provider, so it must not be counted as provider-reported in summary
blocked record in summarizeRecords -> NOT counted in providerReportedTotal/providerReportedCount; WHY: a blocked dispatch never called the provider, so it must not inflate provider totals
buildBlockedBudgetRecord -> record.privacy.promptStored===false and transcriptStored===false; WHY: blocked records still obey the privacy contract
buildBlockedBudgetRecord -> record.authority.mode===local, receiptId===null; WHY: local-only authority boundary applies to blocked records

adversarial.desc: buildBlockedBudgetRecord with a forged budgetPolicyId containing special chars (newlines, quotes, unicode) -> still passes validateUsageLedgerRecord; WHY: policy id from env could contain arbitrary strings, must not break validator
buildBlockedBudgetRecord called with null estimateRecordId (preflight failed) -> still produces a valid record with supersedesRecordIds=[]; WHY: preflight returning null is a documented code path
buildBlockedBudgetRecord output deep-scanned by scanForbiddenFields -> returns zero hits; WHY: blocked records must not accidentally include forbidden fields (totalTokens, secrets, etc.)

items.title: Fail-closed pre-spawn guard in the Claude seam
items.context: In runClaudeCodeRealLeafDispatch (lattice-dispatch.ts), inside the existing isUsageLedgerEnabled() gate and AFTER the preflight estimate: resolveHardBudget; if a budget is set AND isOverHardBudget(preflight estimate): append buildBlockedBudgetRecord, SKIP the spawnSync, and return a blocked dispatch result (do not call the provider). If no budget is set (or estimate within budget), proceed exactly as today. All budget work in try/catch; a budget-check error must NOT wrongly block (on error, proceed as today). Budget UNSET or flag OFF => byte-identical to current dispatch.

happy.desc: Guard active + budget set + estimate OVER budget -> spawnSync is NOT called, blocked record appended to ledger, function returns a blocked dispatch result; WHY: core fail-closed behavior -- must skip provider call when over budget
Guard active + budget set + estimate UNDER budget -> spawnSync IS called, no blocked record, proceeds as normal; WHY: within-budget dispatch must not be impeded
Guard active + no budget env set -> proceeds to spawnSync exactly as today, no budget code side-effects; WHY: unset budget must be a no-op within the enabled ledger path

edge.desc: Ledger OFF (isUsageLedgerEnabled()===false) -> no resolveHardBudget call, no budget check, spawnSync called with original args, byte-identical to pre-budget code; WHY: OFF path must have zero budget side-effects
Guard active + budget set + estimate EXACTLY equal to budget -> proceeds (not blocked); WHY: boundary condition -- block is strict-exceed only (estimate > budget, not >=)
Budget check error (resolveHardBudget or isOverHardBudget throws) -> proceeds to spawnSync as if no budget; WHY: fail-open on error -- a budget-check crash must not wrongly block dispatch

Blocked dispatch result carries well-formed structure (exitCode, stdout indicators) that downstream handlers can distinguish from a normal dispatch; WHY: callers must know the dispatch was budget-blocked, not a provider error

adversarial.desc: resolveHardBudget throws mid-check after preflight succeeded -> try/catch catches, proceeds to spawn, no blocked record; WHY: budget code is inside try/catch, error must not propagate to dispatch caller or wrongly block

buildBlockedBudgetRecord throws (validator rejects assembled record) -> try/catch catches, proceeds to spawn rather than crashing; WHY: a broken blocked-record builder must fail open (proceed), never fail closed (block without record)
Budget env set to extreme value (LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS="1") + non-empty prompt -> blocked; estimate of even a tiny prompt exceeds 1 token; WHY: minimum budget stress test

appendUsageRecord for blocked record throws (fs error) -> guard catches, still returns blocked result (does not proceed to spawn); WHY: once the block decision is made, a write failure must not revert the decision and call the provider

items.title: Regression safety: unset/OFF byte-identical + block only when configured+exceeded
items.context: Tests/assertions: (a) ledger flag OFF => no budget code runs, dispatch byte-identical (spawn happens); (b) flag ON but no hard-budget env => decision proceeds, budgetPolicyId=null, spawn happens (byte-identical control flow); (c) flag ON + hard budget set + estimate over budget => a decision.kind=blocked record is written AND the provider spawn is SKIPPED AND a blocked result is returned; (d) flag ON + budget set + estimate under budget => proceeds + spawns. Prove the block only triggers in case (c).

happy.desc: QUADRANT A: ledger flag OFF -> buildClaudeSpawnArgs returns ["--print", promptFile] (original literal args), no resolveHardBudget/isOverHardBudget called, spawnSync runs, dispatch byte-identical to pre-budget code; WHY: OFF path must produce zero observable difference from the pre-story baseline

QUADRANT B: ledger ON + no LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS env -> resolveHardBudget returns null, isOverHardBudget never called, dispatch proceeds, budgetPolicyId=null on any records, spawn happens; WHY: budget-unset + ledger-on is the common production path before budget adoption

QUADRANT C: ledger ON + LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS=1000 + estimate=2000 (over) -> blocked record with decision.kind=blocked written, spawn SKIPPED, returns blocked dispatch result; WHY: the ONLY quadrant where block fires -- proves positive case
QUADRANT D: ledger ON + LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS=5000 + estimate=2000 (under) -> no blocked record, spawn proceeds, normal dispatch result; WHY: within-budget must not be impeded

edge.desc: QUADRANT A vs B spawn-args comparison: OFF produces ["--print",promptFile], ON produces ["--print",promptFile,"--output-format","json"]; WHY: the ONLY difference between A and B is the output-format flag -- control flow and side-effects are otherwise identical
QUADRANT C: blocked record supersedesRecordIds contains the preflight estimateRecordId; WHY: the blocked record must supersede the estimate so summary does not double-count

QUADRANT C: blocked dispatch result has sufficient structure for the caller to distinguish budget-block from provider-error or timeout; WHY: downstream error handling must not confuse a budget block with a crash
QUADRANT D boundary: estimate exactly equals budget (estimate==budget) -> proceeds (quadrant D not C); WHY: block is strict-exceed (>), not >=

adversarial.desc: QUADRANT C with preflight failure (ledgerHandle===null): budget still resolves and blocks, but blocked record has supersedesRecordIds=[]; WHY: preflight null is documented path; budget block must still fire even without an estimate record to supersede
Budget-check throws in any quadrant -> dispatch proceeds (fail-open); WHY: the try/catch around budget code must catch and proceed, never propagate to caller or block without a record

Rapid sequential dispatches with same budget env: each dispatch independently resolves budget from env, no stale state; WHY: resolveHardBudget must be stateless (reads env each time), no caching of previous result

items.title: Smoke/test suite wired + no regression
items.context: Add packages/main/src/tasks/usage-ledger-budget-smoke.ts (follow existing *-smoke.ts pattern; ✓/✗, non-zero exit; temp dir, no repo pollution), wired as npm test:usage-ledger-budget. Cover the policy resolution, the over-budget predicate, buildBlockedBudgetRecord validation, the blocked record appended + summary treatment (a blocked record is not provider-reported usage), and the fail-closed-only-when-configured behavior (simulated, since a live spawn can't run). Assert usage-ledger still imports ZERO other modules. Build green; full ledger suite (usage-ledger/-adapter/-estimate/-diagnostics/-dispatch) no regression; node bin/lattice.js validate.

happy.desc: npm run test:usage-ledger-budget runs usage-ledger-budget-smoke.ts and exits 0 when all assertions pass; WHY: the smoke must be wired as a named npm script and produce a green exit

usage-ledger-budget-smoke.ts follows existing *-smoke.ts pattern: uses temp dir, prints pass/fail with checkmark/cross, exits non-zero on first failure; WHY: pattern consistency for CI + operator readability
tsc --noEmit passes (build green) after all changes; WHY: new exports/imports must not break the TypeScript build
node bin/lattice.js validate passes; WHY: Lattice self-validation must remain green after adding new code

edge.desc: Full existing ledger smoke suite (usage-ledger, usage-ledger-adapter, usage-ledger-estimate, usage-ledger-diagnostics, usage-ledger-dispatch) all still pass with zero regressions; WHY: new budget code must not break any existing ledger tests

usage-ledger module (core/usage-ledger/) static import analysis: imports ZERO modules outside core/usage-ledger/ and node builtins; WHY: zero-cross-module-import invariant is load-bearing for the one-way seam

budget-smoke covers: resolveHardBudget valid/invalid/unset, isOverHardBudget true/false/boundary, buildBlockedBudgetRecord validation, blocked-record-not-provider-reported in summary, fail-closed-only-when-configured behavior; WHY: the smoke must exercise all budget-related acceptance invariants
Smoke test uses temp directory and cleans up after itself; no files left in repo working tree; WHY: test pollution prevention

adversarial.desc: Run budget smoke test with LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS already set in ambient env -> smoke overrides or isolates env within test, does not leak ambient budget state into assertions; WHY: CI environments may have budget env vars set; smoke must be hermetic
Run budget smoke test twice in rapid succession -> both runs pass, no temp-dir collision or stale state; WHY: idempotency -- smoke must not leave state that breaks the next run

Import graph audit: dispatch-usage.ts new exports (resolveHardBudget, isOverHardBudget, buildBlockedBudgetRecord) are imported ONLY by lattice-dispatch.ts and the smoke test, never by other modules; WHY: prevent uncontrolled coupling of budget internals
